preamble: In the Galician gheada the voiced velar stop /ɡ/ is replaced by a back fricative, and one of its realizations is the voiceless uvular fricative [χ]. Coastal villages prefer velar, pharyngeal or occasional uvular fricatives, which are always voiceless; an acoustic survey counted unvoiced uvular [χ] in 8.3% of gheada tokens. The change is confined to western Galician.

examples.note: Coastal speakers use velar, pharyngeal or occasional uvular voiceless fricatives; Wikipedia transcribes the commonest variant as pharyngeal, gato [ˈħatʊ].

examples.from: /ɡ/ of the test words in Labraña-Barrero & van Oosterzee (2003)
examples.to: unvoiced uvular fricative [χ] in 8.3% of tokens
examples.note: Unvoiced pharyngeal [ħ] was the commonest outcome at 27.8%, and unvoiced velar [x] reached 23%.

sources: Labraña-Barrero, S., & van Oosterzee, C. (2003). An Acoustic Approach to Galician Gheada. Proceedings of the 15th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, Barcelona, 945–948. https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/icphs-proceedings/ICPhS2003/papers/p15_0945.pdf
